julia (Docs): Noticed a confusing example on /v1/generate: the curl snippet uses "max_tokens" while the rest of the page documents "max_new_tokens". Customers are getting mismatched expectations. Can we align and add a short migration note?

raj (API): Ugh, that's on me. We changed the parameter name in the backend last quarter but the docs snippet wasn't updated. The server accepts both for backwards compatibility, but our examples should show the canonical "max_new_tokens" to avoid confusion.

mike (SDK): If server accepts both, should we add a one-liner explaining equivalence? E.g., "max_tokens (deprecated) -> max_new_tokens (preferred)" and show a minimal mapping snippet. I can update SDK examples to only use "max_new_tokens".

julia (Docs): Yes please. Proposed blurb: "Note: legacy client code and some older docs may show \"max_tokens\". The canonical parameter name is \"max_new_tokens\". Both are accepted, but update parsing to use \"max_new_tokens\" for future compatibility." Keep it short and link to migration guide.

claire (QA): Also the current request/response example in the page includes an example response with an enum field "stop_reason" set to "eos" but our runtime returns "stop" in some models. This mismatch will break validation tests. Can we standardize the example to show "stop"?

raj (API): Good catch. The stop_reason values were normalized in the runtime but docs stayed stale. Standard value is now "stop" and "length". I'll update the API contract note.

mike (SDK): I'll change the JS/Python snippets to use "max_new_tokens" and to access the response as `response.output[0].content[0].text` (our SDK shape) and add a tiny example comment about checking `stop_reason === 'stop'`.

julia (Docs): Can you paste the corrected minimal snippets here so I can drop them into the PR? Keep curl + Python + a one-line mapping example.

mike (SDK): Curl:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"model":"base-1","prompt":"Say hi","max_new_tokens":16}'
```Python (pseudo):```python
resp = client.generate(model="base-1", prompt="Say hi", max_new_tokens=16)
print(resp.output[0].content[0].text)  # uses stop_reason == 'stop' or 'length'
```Mapping:```json
{"max_tokens":"legacy", "max_new_tokens":"preferred"}```

julia (Docs): Perfect. I'll add a short migration link: /docs/migrations/max-tokens. Also adding a tiny JSON Schema snippet so the docs linter flags mismatches (schema includes max_new_tokens as integer).

claire (QA): Ran a quick smoke test against staging with the new page preview, examples align with the staging responses. No schema errors in the example set.

deploy-bot: docs-build: succeeded (job 6001) — preview: https://deploy-preview-1420--docs.redwood.ai/reference/generate

mike (SDK): PR opened with snippets + migration blurb + schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1420. Requesting review from @julia and @raj.

julia (Docs): Reviewing now. Tiny nit: make the mapping JSON use descriptive keys in the sentence: "(legacy: \"max_tokens\") -> preferred: \"max_new_tokens\"". Otherwise LGTM.

mike (SDK): Updated text and pushed. CI passed.

julia (Docs): Approved and merged. Adding a changelog note under "Docs updates" for this week.

mike (SDK): Filing follow-up to add a docs unit test that compares example parameter names against SDK canonical usage (infra#799).

julia (Docs): Closing thread. Thanks everyone. If customers report parsing issues we'll add a FAQ note. :sparkles:
